run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T23:15:25Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy (otel-demo) is firing because a rising share of requests through the proxy end in HTTP 504 after a ~15 s wait. The proxy's errors are 504s on its own 'ingress' spans (http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR, durations 14.9998-15.0009 s), and its child 'router frontend egress' span to frontend shows the same 15 s with no upstream status, so the proxy is where the error rate is measured, not where the failure originates. The failure path leads to the cart service's dependency on valkey-cart:6379. Cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' at 23:13:27.940Z and then 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 23:15:44Z (normal GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync lines run up to 23:15:42), and its Deployment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379. A second, independent client on another node fails the same dependency: the otel-collector's redisreceiver series for valkey-cart stop producing new samples around 23:15-23:19Z, although that collector pod is healthy (~230 MB/300Mi, ~0.04 cores, 0 restarts). Cart's own error spans are POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart; frontend's own spans grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and the /api/cart and /api/checkout route spans error; checkout's oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder error, all after the redis loss. I could not determine why the valkey endpoint stopped serving: pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is Running and Ready (no probes configured), restarted 0 times since 22:42:22Z, its cgroup is far below its limits (~3.9 MB working set, ~5.7 MB max usage vs 10Mi; ~0.002-0.0036 cores vs 10m), no OOMKilled/Evicted events exist, the valkey-cart Endpoints still resolve to 100.96.2.228:6379, and all nodes are Ready without pressure. Because the valkey-side mechanism (process wedged inside a running container vs a path problem to its pod IP) is not evidenced — valkey-cart and otel-collector produced no readable log lines in the window, and the NetworkPolicy query returned no data rather than an empty result — the causal claim is a hypothesis and the conclusion is partial. Background error rates (ad, fraud-detection, recommendation ~1.1 per 5m; accounting and payment 0; frontend-proxy 0-3.33 per 5m before 23:13) are unrelated noise and not the cause.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span metric shows the error burst: sum by span_name,status_code of increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m]) for span_name="ingress" reads 0 at 22:56:28Z, 3.33 at 23:01:28Z, 1.11 at 23:05:28Z, 3.33 at 23:11:28Z, then 170 at 23:16:28Z, 438.89 at 23:21:28Z and 216.32 at 23:26:28Z, while span_name="router frontend egress" stayed 0 on STATUS_CODE_ERROR throughout.

The frontend-proxy error spans are 504 timeouts: five frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans between 23:19:55Z and 23:19:59Z carry error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR with durations 15000906, 15000607, 15000218, 14999973 and 14999846 microseconds, and each child 'router frontend egress' span to frontend runs the same ~15.0 s with http.status_code=0.

Whole trace fe75208591425f5a9d17b5773a240de7 (23:19:55Z) contains load-generator user_view_cart -> load-generator GET (504, ERROR, 15.002232 s) -> frontend-proxy ingress (504, ERROR, 15.000906 s) -> frontend-proxy router frontend egress (error=true, http.status_code=0, 15.000549 s) -> frontend GET (http.status_code=200, 15.000476 s); the returned view shows no span below frontend, so the timeout is visible at the proxy but its internal cause is not present in this trace view.

Cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' at 2026-11-16T23:13:27.9403003Z, the earliest redis-connectivity line in its retained logs from 22:45Z, with no other matching line before it.

Cart logged normal 'GetCartAsync called with userId=...' and 'AddItemAsync called ...' lines roughly every second up to 23:15:42.940Z, then 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' at 23:15:44.139444Z interleaved with 'Error status code ... raised.', repeating through the retained stream (last matching line 23:22:01.242053Z).

The cart Deployment's environment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, so cart's 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' lines name the valkey-cart Service as the failing dependency; the same Deployment has limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi with ready=1 and available=1.

An independent client on another node also lost valkey-cart: increase(redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="user_main_thread"}[2m]) from the otel-collector's redisreceiver is 0.0311 at 23:11:25Z and 0.0398 at 23:13:25Z, drops to 0.0109 at 23:15:25Z, is 0 at 23:17:25Z and 23:19:25Z, and the series returns no further points; redis_memory_peak_bytes likewise stops changing at 1726344 from 23:15:25Z onward.

The otel-collector that sources those redis_* series is healthy and unchanged across the window: pod otel-collector-564d9c7987-vpmw7 container opentelemetry-collector is ready with restartCount 0 (running since 22:42:16Z), working set stays 225-235 MB against a 300Mi limit, and CPU rate moves from ~0.041 to ~0.023-0.030 cores without a restart.

Cart and its callers report their own errors after the redis loss: STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase per 5m rises from 5.87 at 23:18Z to roughly 26-31 for cart spans 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart'; frontend spans 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'POST /api/cart', 'GET /api/cart' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' error; checkout spans 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' error from 23:21Z.

Background error levels before 23:13Z differ by orders of magnitude from the incident: per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase per 5m over 22:35-23:31Z was 0 for accounting and payment, 0-1.11 for ad, fraud-detection and recommendation, 0-3.33 for frontend-proxy, versus 100-140 for frontend and 53-437 for frontend-proxy from 23:15Z.

The valkey-cart pod is not crash-looping or OOM-killed: pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is phase Running with condition Ready=True, container valkey-cart ready=true with restartCount 0, state running since 2026-11-16T22:42:22Z, lastState empty, image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine, and it declares no liveness or readiness probe, so 'Ready' does not prove the process was serving.

valkey-cart's cgroup was not resource-saturated while it stopped serving: container_memory_working_set_bytes stays 3.55-4.03 MB (22:53-23:27Z), container_memory_max_usage_bytes peaks at 5.5-5.7 MB against a 10Mi limit, container CPU rate stays 0.0017-0.0036 cores against a 10m limit, and the CFS throttled-period ratio stays 0.01-0.06.

The valkey-cart Service and Endpoints still route to the pod: Service valkey-cart declares port 6379 targetPort 6379 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, and Endpoints valkey-cart has a ready address 100.96.2.228 on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae targeting pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr port 6379. Whether a NetworkPolicy could block that path is unknown, because the NetworkPolicy query in namespace otel-demo returned no data.

Node-level failure is not supported: all five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False; and the product-catalog pod on the same node as cart and valkey-cart (i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) answered oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct in 100-111 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 at 23:19:55Z.

Cart's own CPU and memory rose after the redis connection was lost, not before: container_memory_working_set_bytes for container cart is 59.9 MB at 23:13:25Z, 81.7 MB at 23:15:25Z, 88.1 MB at 23:17:25Z and 97.4 MB at 23:23:25Z, and CPU rate rises from ~0.006-0.011 to 0.026-0.032 cores, still below its 45m limit; pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 remains Running and ready with restartCount 0.

The flagd-injected 'cartFailure' fault is not supported as this cause: ConfigMap flagd-config shows every flag including cartFailure at defaultVariant "off", and the observed cart failure is a redis-connectivity message rather than a flag-declared cart failure; the flag state flagd actually served at 23:13Z could not be read, so this is rejected as unevidenced rather than proven absent at runtime.

The fault originates at the valkey-cart pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr: it stopped serving its clients between 23:13:27Z (cart's 'Connection failed. Disposing the object') and about 23:19Z (last otel-collector redisreceiver sample) while staying Running/Ready without restart, with its cgroup far below its limits and its Endpoints correct — consistent with the redis process becoming unresponsive inside a healthy-looking container, though the specific internal mechanism is not evidenced.

The span-derived series for cart and frontend-proxy both fall to 0, including STATUS_CODE_UNSET, at 23:26:00Z with data_as_of 23:26:00Z, which is absence of spanmetric data rather than evidence that traffic or errors stopped.

The flagd Deployment was changed during the window independently of this failure: ReplicaSet flagd-c47676d99 (created 22:42:14Z) now has replicas 0 while flagd-75c6477d68 (created 22:43:59Z) holds the ready replica, and pod flagd-75c6477d68-8drxp started at 22:43:59Z, about 31 minutes before cart's first redis error, so nothing ties that rollout to the cart/valkey failure.

gaps: No Prometheus rule named RequestErrorRate was returned: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data with result_count 0, so the alert's exact expression, evaluation window and the series behind 'current: 1.0888888888888888' are unknown.

valkey-cart's container produced no readable log lines (fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data, 0 lines, for 22:40-22:50Z and for 22:45-23:31Z), so valkey's own error output — the decisive evidence for why it stopped serving — is missing.
The otel-collector pod's container logs returned status no_data (0 lines) for 23:05-23:31Z, so its redisreceiver error text (dial/lookup/refused detail) could not be read.
The NetworkPolicy query in namespace otel-demo returned status no_data rather than an empty list, so I cannot state whether a NetworkPolicy exists or blocks traffic to valkey-cart:6379.

No exec or port-probe capability exists in this Run, so I could not test TCP connectivity to 100.96.2.228:6379 or read redis INFO/maxclients at 23:13-23:31Z; whether the redis process was wedged, out of client slots, or unreachable at the network level remains undetermined.

Kubernetes objects are visible only in their state at query time and change history is not integrated, so I cannot verify whether the valkey-cart Service, Endpoints or Deployment spec changed around 23:13Z.

Cart and frontend-proxy logs stop at 23:22:01Z and 23:22:03Z respectively and span-derived metrics stop at 23:26Z, so the state of the fault after ~23:22Z is unknown; no recovery was observed while the alert was firing.
No STATUS_CODE_ERROR series were returned for currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote, shipping or load-generator, so their error state is unknown rather than zero.

Events show repeated kubelet 'FailedKillPod'/'Killing' warnings (counts 30 and 75 since 2026-11-15T10:14:49Z, last 23:18:15Z) for the previous cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s with 'KillContainer ... context deadline exceeded'; that pod no longer exists and could not be read, and I cannot tie it to the valkey fault, so it remains an unexplained node/container-runtime symptom.

Traces and trace-id lookups returned no cart spans under error=true or otel.status_code=ERROR (status no_data), so cart's own error spans were observed only through its span metrics, not through sampled traces.
next_steps: Exec into valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr and run redis-cli PING and INFO (connected_clients, maxclients, blocked_clients, rdb_last_bgsave_status) to distinguish a wedged server from a network-path failure.

Read the valkey-cart container's stdout directly from the node/containerd around 23:13-23:19Z to check for fork/save, maxclients or memory errors, since kubectl logs --previous is unavailable (restartCount 0).
Check the alerting rule definition for RequestErrorRate to confirm which metric, series and evaluation window produced the reported value 1.0888888888888888.

Inspect kubelet/containerd health on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, source of the repeating FailedKillPod DeadlineExceeded events for cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s, in case a container-runtime stall also affects the valkey-cart container.

If valkey-cart is found to hit memory or persistence failures, consider raising its limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) and adding a readiness probe; current cAdvisor data shows no saturation, so that is a configuration risk, not an evidenced cause.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
